title: Triple pasting of normalized open product comparisons
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $B$ a scheme; all schemes and morphisms over $B$ may be arbitrary. Work on small pro-etale sites with the ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories $D_A(V)$ and the actual pullbacks, derived tensor, pullback composition, tensor/pullback comparisons, section-normalized open units $\eta^v$ and unique-left-adjoint open composition comparisons of [def-sf-finite-open-tensor-operations]. For open immersions $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$ over $B$ and $K\in D_A(X)$, $L\in D_A(Y)$ put $Z=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $T=X\times_BY$, $u=j\times_Bk:T\hookrightarrow Z$, and
$$H_{j,k}(K,L)=L\bar p^*j_!K\otimes_A^LL\bar q^*k_!L,\qquad D_{j,k}(K,L)=Lp^*K\otimes_A^LLq^*L,$$
where $\bar p,\bar q$ are the projections of $Z$ and $p,q$ those of $T$; write $F\boxtimes G$ for the derived tensor of the two projection pullbacks. Call an isomorphism $e:H_{j,k}(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!D_{j,k}(K,L)$ normalized if $u^*e=\eta^u_{D_{j,k}(K,L)}\circ r$, where $r:u^*H_{j,k}(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{j,k}(K,L)$ is the canonical pullback/tensor comparison followed by the restricted inverse open units of $j$ and $k$.

Let $l:W\hookrightarrow\bar W$ be a third open immersion over $B$, $M\in D_A(W)$, $v=j\times_Bk\times_Bl$, $H_3=j_!K\boxtimes k_!L\boxtimes l_!M$ and $D_3=K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M$. Suppose four normalized isomorphisms are given: $e_{j,k}$ at $(K,L)$, $e_{k,l}$ at $(L,M)$, $e_{j\times k,l}$ at $(K\boxtimes L,M)$ and $e_{j,k\times l}$ at $(K,L\boxtimes M)$. No formula for them is assumed. Define $F$ by first $e_{j,k}\boxtimes1$ and then $e_{j\times k,l}$, and $G$ by first $1\boxtimes e_{k,l}$ and then $e_{j,k\times l}$. The expressions include the canonical projection-pullback tensor comparisons and are regarded as maps $H_3\to v_!D_3$ by the derived tensor associators, the canonical identification of the iterated fibre products and the normalized open composition comparisons. Then $F$ and $G$ are isomorphisms, $v^*F=v^*G=1_{D_3}$ after these specified identifications, restriction along $v$ is injective on morphisms $H_3\to v_!D'$ for every $D'\in D_A(X\times_BY\times_BW)$, and $F=G$. Here the derived associator is the one represented on flat-term K-flat tensor models by $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, and the tensor comparison under restriction sends these tensor sections to the same sections. No faithfulness of restriction on arbitrary ambient sources is asserted.

proof.text:
Put $a=j\times_Bk$, $b=k\times_Bl$ and $T_3=X\times_BY\times_BW$. Use the left bracketing for $D_3$ and let $r_3:v^*H_3\xrightarrow{\sim}D_3$ be restriction/tensor comparison followed by the three inverse open units. All these units are invertible by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], applicable to arbitrary schemes and constant ring sheaves $A$. The open composition comparisons in [def-sf-finite-open-tensor-operations] preserve these identifications: for composable opens $i,j$, write $\delta:(ji)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*j^*$ and $c:j_!i_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(ji)_!$. The composite unit is $i^*(\eta^j_{i_!N})\circ\eta^i_N$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives
$$i^*j^*(c_N)\circ i^*(\eta^j_{i_!N})\circ\eta^i_N=\delta_{(ji)_!N}\circ\eta^{ji}_N.$$
Thus replacing iterated extension by composite extension introduces exactly the displayed unit, rather than an unspecified automorphism.

source.place: Clause (ii), triple products; agent expansion for the specified normalized open comparisons

proof.text: The two bracketings give the same $r_3$ after the prescribed associator. Indeed the associator and restriction/tensor comparison in the statement send $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ in either order to $x|_{T_3}\otimes(y|_{T_3}\otimes z|_{T_3})$; applying the inverse units replaces the three restricted factors by their original sections. These are precisely the native associator formulas of [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints]. Multilinearity, sheafification, and the direct-sum total tensor extend the equality from these generators to complex maps. The flat-term K-flat model computation and preservation under pullback in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] apply to each projection and open restriction. The equivalence of resolving representatives with the derived category in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] carries this equality to the specified derived comparisons; essential surjectivity in each variable suffices to test the resulting natural maps on these models. Pullback-composition comparisons merely identify the same section pulled back along the same composite projection, by their definition in [def-sf-finite-open-tensor-operations]. Consequently no sign or additional comparison remains in rebracketing $r_3$; no factors are permuted.

source.place: Clause (ii), triple products; agent expansion for the specified normalized open comparisons

proof.text:
Every factor in $F$ and $G$ is an isomorphism: the four $e$'s are so by hypothesis, pullback and tensor functors preserve isomorphisms, and the remaining comparisons are specified isomorphisms. To compute $v^*F$, first restrict the normalization $a^*e_{j,k}=\eta^a_{K\boxtimes L}\circ r_{j,k}$ along $T_3\to X\times_BY$, and tensor it with the restricted third factor. For the next arrow the normalization of $e_{a,l}$ applies $\eta^v_{D_3}$ after $r_{a,l}$. By definition $r_{a,l}$ contains the pullback of $(\eta^a_{K\boxtimes L})^{-1}$ and the inverse unit of $l$. Naturality of the tensor/pullback comparison moves the preceding restricted $e_{j,k}$ inside this tensor. The adjacent $\eta^a$ and $(\eta^a)^{-1}$ cancel. The remaining map is exactly $\eta^v_{D_3}\circ r_3$. Similarly, for $G$ use $b^*e_{k,l}=\eta^b_{L\boxtimes M}\circ r_{k,l}$; the next $r_{j,b}$ contains $(\eta^b_{L\boxtimes M})^{-1}$, which cancels that unit. The remaining map is again $\eta^v_{D_3}\circ r_3$ by step 2. Any open composition comparisons satisfy the unit equation of step 1. Hence
$$v^*F=v^*G=\eta^v_{D_3}\circ r_3,$$
which is $1_{D_3}$ after the specified source and target identifications. This uses only the four normalization equations, with no formula or naturality assumption on the supplied $e$'s.

source.place: Clause (ii), triple products; agent expansion for the specified normalized open comparisons

proof.text:
Let $D'\in D_A(T_3)$ and $h,h':H_3\to v_!D'$ with $v^*h=v^*h'$. Since $F$ is invertible, precomposition with $F^{-1}$ identifies these maps with maps $v_!D_3\to v_!D'$. Full faithfulness of $v_!$, from [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], gives unique $t,t':D_3\to D'$ such that $h\circ F^{-1}=v_!t$ and $h'\circ F^{-1}=v_!t'$. Applying $v^*$ and using equality of the restrictions gives $v^*v_!t=v^*v_!t'$. Naturality of the invertible open unit gives
$$t=(\eta^v_{D'})^{-1}\circ v^*v_!t\circ\eta^v_{D_3}=(\eta^v_{D'})^{-1}\circ v^*v_!t'\circ\eta^v_{D_3}=t'.$$
It follows that $h=h'$. Thus restriction is injective on exactly the asserted hom set. The argument uses the isomorphism $H_3\cong v_!D_3$ just established, not faithfulness on arbitrary ambient sources.

source.place: Clause (ii), triple products; agent expansion for the specified normalized open comparisons

proof.text: Apply step 4 with $D'=D_3$, $h=F$ and $h'=G$. Their restrictions agree by step 3, so $F=G$. Together with their invertibility and the explicit restriction identity from step 3, this proves every clause.
